claims.statement: The semantic corpus consists of six doc_types authored as modular YAML: table, column, metric (10-12 metrics), join_rule, example (15-20 few-shots), and event entries with dates and affected regions/channels.
Every semantic chunk carries metadata with chunk_id, doc_type, table plus tables array, metric_name, aliases, sensitivity (public/internal/restricted_pii), optional additive flag, and updated_at.

Chunking is by semantic unit (one YAML entry equals one chunk) through ingestion, embedding, vector store, and retrieval, rather than fixed-token sliding windows that would split formulas from metric names.

Incremental indexing diffs SHA-256 content hashes into unchanged, toUpsert, and toDelete sets, batch-embeds only new or modified chunks, upserts on chunk_id with updated_at refresh, and reports added/updated/skipped/deleted with token and cost telemetry.

The in-memory BM25 index hot-reloads without server restart by checking MAX(updated_at) and chunk count before each retrieve call and refreshing the index and citation catalog when the store is newer.

Retrieval is a three-leg hybrid fusing dense vector cosine search, lexical BM25 with k1 1.2 and b 0.75 over content plus metric_name plus aliases plus tables, and deterministic alias/identifier matching, combined by weighted RRF with k 60 and weights 1.0/1.0/1.5.
After ranking, join-rule graph expansion automatically fetches join_rule chunks whose tables overlap at least two tables from the top metric/table/column results to prevent fan-out double counting.

The LangGraph retrieve-semantic node uses two-tier extraction separating requested_metrics (business KPIs) from schema_entities (tables/columns/literals); unmatched requested_metrics route to cannot_answer with clarification and no invented formula, while empty requested_metrics queries proceed normally.
Definitional questions use a definition_lookup route that bypasses SQL generation and synthesizes the explanation directly from the retrieved metric or column chunk with citations.

Every answer carries dual citations as a citations array in SQLAnswer and a prepended SQL header comment, validated deterministically for catalog existence, current-context grounding, and metric coverage with up to two self-correction retries to reach 100% validity.

UC-02 acceptance requires Recall@5 at least 0.85 on at least 15 definition queries, EX lift at least 15 points with semantic layer on versus off, 100% valid citations, clarification on unknown terms, and behavior change after incremental reindex of only changed docs.

UC-02 evaluation covers five mandatory cases (alias query, fan-out join trap, direct definition, undefined term including forced-guess refusal, and live definition edit with hot reload) plus dense-only baseline versus hybrid regression reporting recall, EX lift, citation rate, latency, tokens, and cost.

The layer integrates via search_semantic_layer tool, MCP resources for data dictionary and metrics, enableSemanticLayer on/off eval flag, getMetricSpec with additive flag for attribution, PII sensitivity alignment, and few-shot examples kept disjoint from graded questions.

The versioned semantic corpus is six YAML files (tables 12, columns 22, metrics 12, joins 7, examples 18, events 10) indexed by chunkYaml with structured fields folded into content and metadata, with semantic/data_dictionary.md and semantic/metrics.md retained as Markdown fallback defaults and as the source for the semantic://data-dictionary and semantic://metrics gateway resources; Markdown chunking splits ## sections and keeps Table/Tables/Metric/Aliases lead lines in content while [restricted_pii] headers mark withheld sections.

chunkMarkdown splits on ## headings, parses Table/Tables/Metric/Aliases lead lines via parseMetaLine, derives table and tables from each other when only one is present, slugs headings into source:slug chunkIds preserving Vietnamese characters, and tags [restricted_pii] headers as restricted_pii while skipping preamble and empty sections.

indexCorpus is incremental via SHA-256 contentHash over canonical chunk JSON including optional additive: it embeds only dirty chunks in one batch, INSERTs new ids, UPDATEs changed rows with refreshed hash/embedding/updated_at, DELETEs ids absent from the corpus via chunk_id = ANY($1), returns {added, updated, skipped, deleted, embeddingTokens, estimatedCostUsd, durationMs} with heuristic token/cost telemetry, validates every chunk through SemanticChunkMetadataSchema, and runs as an operator tsx module (pnpm semantic:index) against INDEXER_DATABASE_URL using discoverDefaultFiles — the six YAML files in canonical order when semantic YAML exists, otherwise the two Markdown defaults.

Embeddings come from a deterministic 1536-dim L2-normalized fake embedder (FNV-1a plus mulberry32) used by tests/CI, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured by EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID, OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL, EMBEDDING_API_KEY and EMBEDDING_DIM; selectEmbedderFromEnv prefers OpenAI only when model and key are set.

semantic.semantic_chunks stores snake_case metadata plus content, SHA-256 content_hash, updated_at watermark, vector(1536) embedding, and a generated tsvector fts column via immutable_unaccent, served by HNSW cosine and GIN FTS indexes.

Database roles isolate the layer: agent_ro has only USAGE plus chunk-only SELECT on semantic_chunks with no default privileges for future tables, while indexer holds full write grants on semantic tables and zero rights on public.

hybridSearch fuses three legs — pgvector cosine-distance leg fetching max(topK*3,topK) candidates with dense_score, in-memory Okapi BM25 leg over content plus metric/alias/table fields, and deterministic alias/identifier matcher leg — with every leg filtering sensitivity != restricted_pii unless the caller holds data:sensitive via allowRestricted.

Fusion is weighted RRF at k=60 with weights [1.0, 1.0, 1.5] via pure fuseRRF/rrfScore with first-seen tie-breaking and topK truncation followed by join-rule graph expansion that keeps the result within topK, and storage rows map to the camelCase contract shape by splitting comma-joined tables with the fused score plus optional aliasMatched and denseScore attached.

The frozen contract defines SearchSemanticLayer input {query 1..2000 chars, topK 1..20 default 5} and output chunks {chunkId, docType enum of six values table/column/metric/join_rule/example/event, table, tables, metricName, content, score} plus optional aliasMatched and denseScore set by the fusion path.

The gateway exposes search_semantic_layer under data:read scope through the fixed pipeline (auth, scope, zod, skipped SQL stages, injected search, per-chunk redactPII with hit counting, single audit line) with PII redaction applied to every chunk body.

The gateway serves semantic://data-dictionary and semantic://metrics resources from checked-in Markdown under schema:read scope, withholding ## sections ending in [restricted_pii] without data:sensitive via filterResourceSections before PII redaction and audit.

The LangGraph retrieveSemantic node with two-tier requestedMetrics versus schemaEntities guardrail and the deterministic dual JSON plus SQL-header citation validator are implemented in packages/agent, while recall and lift thresholds remain eval criteria rather than runtime checks.

YAML structured fields (formula, sql, caveats, question, citedMetrics, dates, affected regions/channels, grain, primary key, and related column metadata) are appended to chunk content as Label: value lines when absent and merged into stored metadata JSONB alongside the validated contract, and the indexer persists additive and metadata JSONB on both INSERT and UPDATE.

createRetrieveSemantic defaults to topK 8 and dense threshold 0.6, passes through with no search for basic queries, fails closed on missing transport and empty retrieval, bypasses the gate on user formulas, and short-circuits ungrounded terms to cannot_answer with closest metrics and zero SQL.
Metric grounding requires a metric or column chunk trusted by aliasMatched or denseScore at threshold with per-term text overlap for multi-metric questions.
Checkpointed semanticChunks persist chunkId score text plus aliasMatched and denseScore trust signals used by the entry regate.
Definition lookup searches and persists chunks in retrieve but synthesizes in the text-to-SQL entry with sql null and zero executor calls.

Citation validation enforces catalog membership, retrieved-this-turn grounding with column and metric interop, and metric coverage, with sorted header injection, metric-preferring derivation, and repair limited to two retries for unknown or not-retrieved ids.
The text-to-SQL entry derives citations from retrieved ids and fails closed to cannot_answer on persistent citation failure instead of shipping unverified SQL.
Retrieved event chunks feed the UC-03 claim validator as eventIds to ground causal language.
